visual.general_description: Line graph of serum ammonia (umol/L) against hours of admission, with printed values at each marker and labelled arrows for HD session, CVVHD, two TPE sessions, cerebral edema and brain herniation.
visual.detailed_description: White background with dotted gridlines. X axis is titled Hours of Admission with major ticks 0 to 84 every 6 hours; Y axis is titled Ammonia Level (umol/L) with ticks 0 to 1000 every 200. A single black line with filled black circular markers starts at about hour 2 at 40, rises steeply to 810 at about hour 17, dips to 757 (about hour 24), rises through 789 (31), 818 (34), 944 (38) to a peak of 979 at about hour 40, then falls through 777, 740, 660, 571, 551, 534, 490 (to about hour 54), 306 (62) and 325 (64), 260, 261, 242, 240 (to hour 72) and 178, a marker without its own printed label (about 160) and 169, 139 and 135 at about hours 74-82. Each value is printed in a dotted rectangle next to its marker. Red boxed labels with dashed arrows mark HD Session (about hour 19), CVVHD (about hour 35-36), #1 TPE (about hour 41) and #2 TPE (about hour 57). Blue boxed labels with dashed arrows mark Cerebral Edema (about hour 19) and Brain Herniation (about hour 79). No patient name, date or reference-range line is shown.

clinical_significance.statement: Text cites Figure 1 for ammonia falling from a maximum of 979 to 169 umol/L despite intensive treatment while the condition worsened.

evidence.quote: Despite intensive treatment and reduction of the ammonia level from a maximum value of 979 to 169 µmol/L ( Figure 1 ), the patient’s condition continued to deteriorate.

limitations: Figure marker times are plotted on an hours-of-admission axis and are not reconciled with narrative times: the narrative reports decline at twelve hours, a repeat CT with edema six hours later, a head CT at 72 hours showing herniation and brain death declared twelve hours after that, whereas Figure 1 shows Cerebral Edema near hour 19 and Brain Herniation near hour 79.
The text gives 169 umol/L as the reduced ammonia value; the plot continues to lower printed values 139 and 135 afterwards.

The first plotted point (40 at about hour 2) matches the admission ammonia; the plotted 810 at about hour 17 matches the repeat-lab value whose table column is headed 6 Hours; the table header and the plotted hour were not reconciled.
HD Session is a labelled marker in the plot only; the narrative describes CVVHD and TPE, not a separate hemodialysis session. Therapy sessions are marked only by arrows, with no durations.

visual.general_description: Colored schematic of ACLF pathophysiology and potential treatments leading to cerebral edema, with yellow treatment boxes and arrows/T-bars between labelled ellipses.
visual.detailed_description: Cartoon liver (dark red, spotted) labelled ACLF at top center with an intestine drawing below it, a red-blood-cell circle labelled Circulation at right, a pink brain labelled Cerebral Edema at lower left and a small neuron drawing beside it. Pink ellipses read Precipitating Events (with starburst tags Infection, Alcohol, Bleed, Viral Hepatitis), Systemic Inflammation, Impaired Toxins & Ammonia Metabolism and Impaired Blood Brain Barrier. Yellow boxes read Lactulose, Rifaximin, Therapeutic Plasmaphresis and Hemodialysis CRRT; two maroon boxes read Induced Hypocapnia / Pharmacological Coma (above the brain) and Hyperosmolar Therapy / Therapeutic Hypothermia (below the brain). Thin arrows connect precipitating events to ACLF, ACLF to systemic inflammation and impaired ammonia metabolism, ammonia and toxins into Circulation, and systemic inflammation into Circulation. A hollow double-line connector runs from Circulation down to Impaired Blood Brain Barrier, and a large hollow arrow points from there to the brain with Osmotic Gliopathy and Proinflammatory Cytokines above it and Oxidative & Nitrosative Stress, Ion & Water Channel Dysfunction and Neuronal Lactate Accumulation below. Treatment boxes connect to targets with lines ending in T-bars. No patient identifiers, dates, numbers or scale are printed.
